items.note: Hessel Bottom named as the wet meadow at Ostrey Hollow, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest - all three bolded elements present in story 1.
Brant weigh book is named as a document but Section A never gives its 1 January 1897 start nor states that his scale and the station scale agreed. Not creditable from C or D.

1902 complaints are stated, but the item's gate is tripped: the run gives the Hollow-vs-Green comparison as 0.19 (gap 0.19, 3.61 v 3.78) in the narrative and again in its Quantities line. 3.78 minus 3.61 is 0.17; the two gaps are conflated.
1908 committee under Nyle Grigg, sampling January-February-March 1908, wet-hay verdict reported as the committee's finding and then refuted by Bulletin 214.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and the proportional loss across richer herds appear nowhere in Section A.
Emmet's 1929 death is mentioned but not the weigh book passing to Roy Brant in 1929 nor its loan to Ivy Keddie in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd all named; the year does not gate.
From 1915, four Hessel Bottom men hauled over in the summer flush and returned to Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year.
REQUIRED line met with all four elements: another county (Vessey), his own bench, his own glass, and a book never compared with anyone's.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930 stated (fourteen explicitly rejected), Cudd's averages 3.78-3.82 against the station's 3.61, the 0.19 named.

States the same cows on the same hay in the summer months testing 3.80 on another man's glass and 3.61 on the station's - the two-buildings comparison, with the cheesemaker never docking a can killing the watering side.
Rosalie Cudd's 1958 letter with the sixteen-season table is cited, but Section A never states her relation to Jerome; the bolded daughter element (NT-21) is absent.
Strawn is named as the state inspector but Section A gives no Ordell circuit, no 1907-1936 span, no notebook-a-year, and no statement of his independence from the valley.

Section A states that Strawn told the manager he had never found water and never did - the negative water finding at Ostrey Hollow across his tenure. The instrument name (lactometer) is absent but the substantive claim in the bolded clause is made.
The 12 June 1923 burette test and the condemnation of the whole lot are nowhere in Section A; the run filed them into a batch-3 story. The dates appear at C5, which cannot travel into Section A.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure for the deficiency and making no report beyond the condemnation.
Replacement glass ordered 28 June, acknowledged 2 July 1923, and the 1924 average of 3.80 appear only at C5 and D2, not in Section A.
The crate going to the station loft and the notebooks reaching the college library in 1947 are absent from Section A.
40,000,000 x 3.61 percent = 1,444,000 lb, with the 57,760 x 25 cross-check; 44,000,000 and 3.16 both rejected by arithmetic.
40,000,000 x 3.80 percent = 1,520,000 lb, cross-checked at 60,800 x 25.
76,000 lb, given as 5.26 percent of the fat credited and 5.00 percent of the fat delivered, with both denominators named explicitly and NT-20 identified as the wrong base.
$77.93, with the five line items summed; the $77.39 transposition rejected because it does not sum.
Six dozen equals 72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c. (17.6 minus 16.72). Five dozen and 16.27 both rejected with working.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 = 26 years and 42 days (day count verified correct), and 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason for the difference stated for both 1897 and 1923.

Abstention item A02 correctly declined: verdict sentence is cannot be determined from the sources, with the reason (no 1896 intake figure in the station papers, two hearsay figures 200,000 lb apart). The later 0.9-1.1 million range is a lean, not a verdict.
Variable correctly named as the measuring glass - the station pipette broken 8 May 1911, a borrowed one until 10 July; one object changed.
Constants listed well beyond the required three: tester, patrons and cans, herds, hay and pasture, scales, acid, test bottles, bookkeeping.
Tests rose 3.61 to 3.80 for the nine weeks and fell back on the day the station's own measure returned; the six-week error is explicitly rejected on the 63-day span.

Both halves present: hay, watering and theft excluded at once with the cause located in the glass; and limits stated - no size in cubic centimeters, nothing about the bottles or the rest of the outfit, and the lender of the borrowed measure unsettled.
Four reasons given (ledger surplus, 1911 interval, 1923 glass with the 1924 rise, Alder Corners), each attributed across well more than three narrators.
Independence argued explicitly by record, place and witness, and reasons 1-3 named as surviving without the 1958 measurement.

Abstention item A09 asserted. The headline verdict sentence is 'As to the bookkeeper: no.' - a flat verdict in the sheet's own voice with no declining qualifier. The later 'I cannot say he never noticed the line was odd' does not undo it under the key's operational test. The sheet also supplies evidence against its own verdict (Teague raising the station account with Vose in 1916).
Answers the literal question yes, and carries it three ways: complaints at every annual meeting since 1902, the 1919 circular he signed, and the 1926 address.
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913 (with 1911 rejected), the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line signed from 1913, and the 1919 water circular.

Abstention item A03 asserted in the negative: 'no, the sources say he did not know it, and show how he failed to', closed by 'he knew the tests ran low and did not know why'. A verdict either way scores zero here.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: the Alder Corners factory 'built 1913' (corruption-map X34, F055 - the catalogued wrong value is worded 'The factory was built in 1913'). Unhedged, unattributed, reconciled with 1914 by inventing a built-vs-opened distinction no source supports.

Planted error asserted as fact: 'Teague invented the line in 1905' (corruption-map X19, F104/F049 - r05's self-refuting boast; the station-gain line was carried from 1898). Asserted flatly at D2 item 3, contradicting the run's own hedge at D2 item 2.
Gullibility, abstention item A09 (D2 item 3): definite assertion 'As to the bookkeeper: no.' where the sources cannot settle whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries.
Gullibility, abstention item A03 (D3 item 3): definite assertion that the manager did not know the tests were understated, where the sources cannot settle it either way.
